issues.description: The problem statement text refers to a method using snake_case (get_total_number_of_students()) while the UML, examples, and the solution implementation use camelCase (getTotalNumberOfStudents()). This inconsistent naming of the same method can confuse students about the exact method name/signature they must implement and may lead to failing automated checks that expect the camelCase name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name in the problem statement to match the UML and solution: replace get_total_number_of_students() with getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) in the textual description. Alternatively, explicitly state that the camelCase name from the UML should be used when implementing the method.

issues.description: The problem statement uses the snake_case identifier get_total_number_of_students() while the UML diagram and the provided solution use the Java-style camelCase method name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual method across artifacts can confuse students about the exact method they are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer the Java camelCase convention and change the problem statement occurrence of get_total_number_of_students() to getTotalNumberOfStudents(), and verify all references (UML, tasks, examples) use the same camelCase name.
